asideText: Passwords are generated with your browser's cryptographic random generator. Nothing is sent or stored.

faq.a: It uses crypto.getRandomValues, your browser's cryptographically secure random generator — suitable for passwords, unlike Math.random.
Longer is stronger. 16+ characters with all character types enabled resists brute-force attacks for the foreseeable future.
No. Generation happens entirely in your browser. Nothing is sent, stored, or logged anywhere.

whenNotToUse: A strong password still fails if you reuse it or store it in plain text — save generated passwords in a password manager.
Some sites restrict length or symbols; match the site's stated rules if a generated password is rejected.
